documentation.description: Measures the functional cooperation between modules of a package via information flow. Considers module invocations and data consumption (imports).
documentation.formula: IFC-P(P) = (2 * sum(F_ij)) / (m * (m - 1)), where F_ij = 1 if module i invokes module j or consumes its data.

interpretation.0.8-1.0: Excellent - High functional coupling within package

documentation.description: Measures the number of connected components within a package. A connected component represents a group of modules related through dependencies, shared data, model files, or ML library usage. Lower values indicate better cohesion (ideally 1 component).
documentation.formula: LPCML(P) = |CC(G_P)|, where G_P = (V, E) is the undirected dependency graph. V = first-level elements (modules/subpackages), E = edges exist when elements share resources (non-empty intersection).

interpretation.1: Excellent - All modules form a single cohesive unit
interpretation.2-3: Acceptable - Package has few disconnected subgroups
interpretation.>5: Poor - Highly fragmented package, refactoring needed

documentation.description: Measures the structural sharing of data or models between modules of the same package. High values indicate that modules within a package are tightly coupled through shared resources.
documentation.formula: PDSC(P) = (2 * sum(Q_ij)) / (m * (m - 1)), where Q_ij = 1 if modules i and j access or modify the same data structures or resources.

documentation.description: Measures how focused a package is on a specific ML pipeline function. Evaluates the concentration of ML-related modules within a package and penalizes packages that span multiple pipeline stages. Higher PFP indicates better package cohesion and adherence to single responsibility principle.
documentation.formula: PFP = (n_ml / n_total) × CF, where CF = 1 - ((n_stages - 1) / (MAX_STAGES - 1)). n_ml = ML modules in package, n_total = total modules, n_stages = unique stages detected, CF = concentration factor that penalizes stage dispersion.

interpretation.High (0.8-1.0): Excellent package purity - focused on single pipeline function with high ML content
interpretation.Low (0.4-0.59): Poor purity - package handles multiple stages or has low ML content, refactoring recommended
interpretation.Moderate (0.6-0.79): Acceptable purity - package is reasonably focused but has room for improvement
interpretation.Very Low (0.0-0.39): Critical purity issues - package lacks clear purpose, immediate refactoring needed

documentation.name: Package Functional Purity
references: Single Responsibility Principle - Clean Code by Robert C. Martin
